cards.title: Compute is a system, not just a chip
cards.summary: Huang presented Blackwell alongside networking and rack-scale systems for larger AI workloads.
cards.interpretation: For builders, memory and communication can matter as much as nominal compute. Benchmark the entire serving path.
cards.opportunity: Measure latency, memory use and cost per successful task before changing hardware.

cards.title: Packaging models is product work
cards.summary: Huang introduced NIM microservices to package and deploy AI models through standard APIs.
cards.interpretation: Deployment interfaces can turn model capability into something a team can operate. The announcement alone proves no product fit.
cards.opportunity: Prototype one bounded workflow and compare integration effort with your current stack.

cards.title: Simulation is a practice ground
cards.summary: Huang described simulated environments for robot learning and introduced tools for perception and manipulation.
cards.interpretation: If simulation transfers reliably to physical tasks, it could shorten iteration. Real-world safety still needs direct validation.
cards.opportunity: Study sim-to-real failures and test one task in both environments.

cards.title: Better data deserves a seat at the table
cards.summary: Wang argued that high-quality datasets and efficient human feedback were bottlenecks as compute and models grew.
cards.interpretation: Treat dataset quality as engineering work. More data helps only when it addresses the failures you actually observe.
cards.opportunity: Build a small error taxonomy and show how targeted labels change held-out performance.

cards.title: A scaling forecast is still a forecast
cards.summary: Wang forecast growth in compute and data, with new model capabilities emerging from scale.
cards.interpretation: Scaling may improve capability, but a historical prediction does not guarantee every task improves or every business benefits.
cards.opportunity: Compare a smaller and larger model on the same representative evaluation set.

cards.title: Start with the workflow, then adapt the model
cards.summary: The keynote summary describes pretrained models and task-specific tuning as routes for enterprises without in-house model expertise.
cards.interpretation: A pretrained model can reduce the starting cost. Owning evaluation and domain context remains your team’s responsibility.
cards.opportunity: Choose one costly repeatable task; test the baseline before considering fine-tuning.

cards.title: Seeing should lead to acting
cards.summary: Li describes spatial intelligence as processing visual information, predicting outcomes and acting in the physical world.
cards.interpretation: If systems connect perception to reliable action, useful applications may extend beyond text. Reliability and human needs remain constraints.
cards.opportunity: Try a perception task with changing viewpoints and document where the system fails.
